title: The cup (Matthew 20:17–28)
hookLine: a mother asks for thrones for her sons; he asks, can you drink my cup?
tomorrow: why would Jesus ask two blind men what they want?

lines: THE BEST SEATS, FOR HER BOYS.
cards: Somewhere, right now, a parent is writing an email to a coach about playing time. Here's the oldest version of that email.
Jesus is on the road up to Jerusalem, and he has just told the twelve, plainly, that he'll be handed over and killed, and rise on the third day.
Then the mother of Zebedee's children kneels in front of him, her two sons beside her: James and John. She has one request.
"Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom." The best seats. For her boys.

teach.h: YE KNOW NOT WHAT YE ASK.
teach.b: Jesus answers the sons, not the mother.
"Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of?" The cup, in his mouth, is what he just described on the road. They answer at once: "We are able."
He tells them they will drink it, but the seats at his right and left are not his to give.
Then the other ten hear about it, and they're furious with the two brothers. So now all twelve are arguing about rank. Jesus calls them together.
The rulers of the nations lord it over people, he says, and the great ones use their power.
Then the line this day keeps: "But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister." Minister, here, means servant.
And he points to himself: "Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many."
One to tell a friend: in Matthew, the brothers ask for seats, and he offers a cup. He answers the whole quarrel by describing his own life.

how: Some churches read Matthew 20:28 when they commission people for service, and the word minister, from this passage's 'let him be your minister', is still a name for church leaders in some Protestant churches.

s: in Matthew, James and John make the request for the seats themselves
in Matthew their mother kneels and asks for them; Jesus answers the sons.

they will drink his cup, but the seats are not his to give.

games.q: you've just been picked to lead a group project, and two classmates are openly annoyed. by Jesus' answer to the ten, what does leading look like?
o: take the jobs nobody wants, first.
remind them who was chosen to lead.
step down so nobody feels left out.
games.why: Jesus doesn't abolish greatness; he redefines it: whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister, your servant.

practice: Think of one person whose week you could make lighter with a small, unglamorous job: a ride, a dish, an errand, an hour of help. Write them a short text with a plain offer, I can do this for you, and no reason to notice you in it.
Send it now, or keep it ready to send when the sit ends.
